analysis.investment_thesis: Engineers India is a decent-quality business with ~20% ROIC and near-zero debt, but the Magic Formula rejects it on valuation: EBIT of INR 514 Cr against an EV of ~INR 13,484 Cr yields just ~3.8% earnings yield — far below the 12% minimum for attractiveness. Good business, wrong price.
key_strengths: High ROIC ~20% (EBIT 514 Cr / Invested Capital ~2,590 Cr), sustained over multiple years
Near-zero leverage (Debt/Equity 0.01; total debt only INR 22 Cr) — fortress balance sheet
Government PSU with 51% promoter ownership provides stable order pipeline in hydrocarbons/infra
key_risks: Earnings yield too low (~3.8%) — Magic Formula demands >12%; stock is priced for perfection
Revenue has been flat-to-declining since 2020 (INR 3,237 Cr → 3,088 Cr), no growth engine visible
Free cash flow severely lags net profit (FCF INR 68 Cr vs. net profit INR 580 Cr in 2025) — large working capital drag
red_flags: Other income (INR 160 Cr) contributes ~28% of net profit — treasury/investment income inflates PAT vs. true operating earnings
Operating CF of INR 109 Cr vs net profit INR 580 Cr — FCF conversion of ~12% is very poor; negative FCF in 2023
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: Enterprise Value = Market Cap (13,601) + Debt (22) − Cash (139) = ~INR 13,484 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income 2025) = INR 514 Cr. Earnings Yield = 514/13,484 = 3.8% — well below the 6% floor, let alone the 12%+ threshold I look for. ROIC = EBIT / Invested Capital (~2,590 Cr) = ~20%, which is decent but not exceptional. The Magic Formula demands both metrics be high; here the valuation leg collapses the thesis entirely.

The quality picture has some real cracks beneath the surface. Net profit of INR 580 Cr looks impressive, but strip out INR 160 Cr of other income (treasury returns on a cash-heavy balance sheet) and the operating story is more modest. Revenue has effectively stagnated since 2020, and free cash flow conversion is alarming — only INR 68 Cr of FCF against 580 Cr of reported profits, with negative FCF in 2023. At P/E 17.5x with flat revenue growth and poor FCF conversion, the market is pricing in recovery/re-rating that the fundamentals don't yet justify. A Magic Formula investor would pass and wait for a cheaper entry.
